DrinkCountIn.description:
A count typed in rather than tapped up to — the counter, or one
earlier day.

Bounded at 99 as typo protection, not as a drinking limit: either way
it is one evening, and a three-digit number in that box is a slipped
finger, which is worth a 422 rather than a silent hundred rows.
DrinkCountIn.title: DrinkCountIn

DrinkCounterOut.description:
The Today tab's beer counter (ADR-019).

`count` is the drinks since the last reset — the number on the stepper
— not a lifetime total. Every write endpoint returns this same shape,
so the client never has to re-read the counter after changing it.

`volume_l` and `alcohol_grams` are what one tap means, sent rather than
hard-coded in the frontend so the label under the stepper and the
number the report reasons about can never drift apart.
DrinkCounterOut.title: DrinkCounterOut

DrinkDayOut.description:
One local day of beers, as the Beer sheet plots and edits it
(ADR-023, ADR-024).

`count` is the whole day — what was tapped in at the time plus what was
filled in afterwards — and the day is the *server's* local day, which
is why the client is sent the date rather than working one out in the
browser's own zone.

`reported` is how many of those beers an AI report already counted. It
is the floor: those rows stay, because a report describing four beers
must not end up beside a history holding two, so the editor stops its
minus there instead of spending a round trip on a 422.

`editable` is false for today alone, whose beers are the counter's. The
server decides it for the same reason it sends the date: its day
boundary is not necessarily the browser's.
DrinkDayOut.title: DrinkDayOut

ExerciseSessionOut.description:
One session behind a day's load — mirrors
api.services.exercises.ExerciseSession.

`metrics` is an open bag of whatever else Google recorded for the
session, keyed by its own camelCase field name. It is untyped on
purpose: the set varies by activity type and by what the Health API has
shipped, and pinning it down here would mean a schema change every time
the watch learns a new number. The four fields above it are the ones
confirmed live and used for display — see the service module.
ExerciseSessionOut.title: ExerciseSessionOut

HeartRateZoneOut.description:
One heart rate zone over a session: where it starts, and how long was
spent in it.

`lower_bpm` is null only for the lowest zone and `upper_bpm` only for the
highest — they are the ends of the scale, not missing values. The bounds
are derived (the API publishes minutes per zone but not the boundaries
between them); `SessionHeartRateOut.zone_source` says where the seconds
came from.
HeartRateZoneOut.title: HeartRateZoneOut

LatestMeasurementsOut.description:
The last known value of each sparse metric (ADR-018).

Every field is optional and omitted when the metric has never been
recorded — an absent key is "no reading ever", which is not the same as
a reading of zero. The values here are deliberately not folded into
`DailyHealthOut`: a daily row says what was measured *that day*, and a
carried-forward weight in that shape would make the charts draw a flat
line through days nobody stood on the scale.
LatestMeasurementsOut.title: LatestMeasurementsOut

MeasurementOut.description:
One reading of a metric that is not recorded every day, with the day
it was taken. Mirrors api.services.health.Measurement.
MeasurementOut.title: MeasurementOut

MissingMatchOut.description:
Yesterday's fixture from the calendar that the ÖFB log has no game
for — see api/services/matches.py for why that can happen.
MissingMatchOut.title: MissingMatchOut

ScorePointOut.description:
One day's recovery and readiness. Separate from DayPointOut because
the two series end on different days — see analysis.training_load.
ScorePointOut.title: ScorePointOut

SessionHeartRateOut.description:
One tracked session's heart rate trace — mirrors
api.services.heart_rate.SessionHeartRate.

`samples` is `[seconds_from_start, bpm]` pairs, thinned to what a
phone-width chart can draw; `sample_count` is how many readings are
stored behind them, so the client can say how much it is showing.

Empty `samples` means two different things, told apart by `fetched_at`:
with a timestamp, the watch recorded no heart rate for this session;
without one, the sync has not reached it yet (ADR-020 fetches the newest
sessions first, a bounded number per run).
SessionHeartRateOut.title: SessionHeartRateOut

SkipIn.description:
Mark a scheduled session as done-or-not.

A state, not a toggle: the dashboard sends what it wants to be true, so
a double tap or a replayed request lands on the same answer. `ref_id` is
the natural key the listed session carries — `oefb_game_id` for a match,
the Google event id for a training.
SkipIn.title: SkipIn

TrainingStatusOut.description:
Mirrors api.analysis.training_load.TrainingStatus. Form travels as a
percentage of fitness because the load unit (Active Zone Minutes) does
not carry the ±25 TSB bands cycling uses.
TrainingStatusOut.title: TrainingStatusOut

schema.title: Response List Upcoming Events Calendar Events Get

get.description: The drinks logged since the last daily report claimed them.

put.description:
Set the counter to a number typed straight into the tile — four taps
is fine, eleven is not.

Idempotent, unlike the two above: it says what the counter should read,
so a replayed request cannot add a beer. Only the drinks no report has
claimed are moved; the difference is added or removed at the newest end.

get.description:
The last `days` local days ending today, newest first, empty ones
included — the Beer sheet's chart and its editable day rows read the
same list.

Today is in it so the chart can plot it, and comes back
`editable: false` because that evening belongs to the counter.

schema.title: Response List Days Drinks Days Get

get.description:
One day, however far back — what the date picker reads when a date is
chosen, so the field opens on the number already stored rather than on a
guess (ADR-024). A day with no beers answers zero, not 404.

put.description:
Fill in (or correct) the beers of one earlier day — the round nobody
remembered to tap in on Saturday (ADR-023).

Idempotent: it carries the number that day should read, so a retry
lands on the same history. The rows it writes are off the counter from
birth, so this cannot move the stepper upwards or feed tonight's report
a beer from last week — it lands on the day it names, which is where
later analysis reads it.

Any past date is accepted, however old — the picker that sends it is a
calendar, not a typed number (ADR-024). 422, with the reason in
`detail`, for the two the service refuses: today or later (that is the
counter's job), and a count below what a report already counted on that
day. A count over 99 is refused a step earlier, by `DrinkCountIn`, the
same slipped-finger guard the counter has.

delete.description:
Minus one: take back the most recent tap that no report has counted
yet. A no-op at zero — the count that comes back says so, and a 404 for
a button the user pressed once too often would be noise.

get.description:
The newest `limit` stored days, newest first. Read a month at a time
from the newest, so a year of history costs about a dozen reads.

schema.title: Response List Daily Health Health Data Daily Get

get.description: The most recently tracked workouts, newest first.

schema.title: Response List Exercises Health Data Exercises Get

get.description:
One tracked session's heart rate trace (ADR-020).

Its own request rather than a field on `/exercises`: a trace is a few
hundred points even after thinning, and the list renders ten sessions
that would each be carrying one nobody has opened. The detail sheet
fetches this when it opens.

404 is "no such session" — a bad id, or one naming a match or training
the watch never recorded. A session that exists but has no readings
answers 200 with an empty `samples`, which is a different thing and the
sheet says so.

The current weight and VO2 max, whichever day they were last measured
on (ADR-018). Separate from `/daily` because it deliberately reaches past
the window `/daily` was asked for: the last weigh-in can be older than
any range the app shows, and it is still the current weight.

Liveness probe. Named /healthz, not /health, so it isn't mistaken for
a sibling of the /health-data routes.

Newest first, undated rows before all of them — Postgres'
`ORDER BY match_date DESC` puts NULLs first, and this keeps its order.

Yesterday's calendar fixture if the ÖFB log has no game that day,
else null. The app shows it as a notice on the Today tab.

schema.title: Response Missing Yesterday Matches Missing Get

get.description: Who the API thinks is calling — the app's check that sign-in worked.

post.description:
Mark a scheduled match or training as missed, or undo that.

Only untracked days are affected in the first place — a day the watch
recorded is scored on what it recorded, and a skip there changes
nothing (see api/services/exercises.py). The 404 is what stops a stale
id becoming a row that silently matches nothing for ever.
